name: Compromised-account / friend scam
shortDescription: A scammer appears to be someone the target knows, often through a compromised account or fake emergency, and pressures them to send money, codes, or take another sensitive action.
recurringStructure: Known-person identity -> urgent, emotional, or account-related claim -> request for money or a security code -> pressure to act before independently verifying.

name: Job / task scam
shortDescription: An unexpected work or simple-task offer that eventually seeks money or sensitive information.
recurringStructure: Unexpected work offer -> easy or repetitive tasks -> apparent earnings or trust-building -> deposit, fee, or sensitive-information request.

name: Relationship / investment scam
shortDescription: A scammer builds personal or romantic trust, or promotes an investment opportunity, before pressuring the target to send money or deposit funds.
recurringStructure: New relationship or investment contact -> trust or profit claims -> move toward money or investing -> deposit or transfer request -> continued pressure or sunk-cost pressure.

name: Bank / government / institution impersonation scam
shortDescription: A scammer pretends to represent a bank, government agency, or other trusted institution and uses authority, fear, or account claims to obtain money, credentials, or security codes.
recurringStructure: Trusted institution identity -> account, legal, security, or payment problem -> authority or urgency pressure -> request for money, credentials, code, or login.

name: Online shopping / marketplace scam
shortDescription: A fake or dishonest buyer or seller abuses an online shopping or marketplace interaction to obtain money, security codes, or off-platform payment.
recurringStructure: Buyer or seller interaction -> unusual payment or verification request -> pressure to leave platform protections or use a supplied link -> money or code loss.

name: Tech support / pop-up scam
shortDescription: A scammer claims a device has a security problem and pressures the target to install software, grant remote access, or pay for unnecessary support.
recurringStructure: Device or security warning -> claimed technical support -> fear or urgency -> remote-access, software-installation, or payment request.

name: Professional-targeted scam
shortDescription: A scam abuses a professional workflow such as recruiting, developer collaboration, invoicing, or business payments to obtain money, credentials, or code execution.
recurringStructure: Professional identity or workflow -> apparently legitimate work, invoice, or collaboration request -> sensitive professional action -> payment, credentials, or software execution.

name: Malicious document / attachment scam
shortDescription: An ordinary-looking document or attachment is used as the lure for malware, credential theft, or another harmful action.
recurringStructure: Ordinary-looking file or document -> reason to open, download, or execute it -> urgency or trusted-workflow framing -> malware, credential, or account risk.
